# three-vat

> Bake a three.js `AnimationClip` into vertex animation textures (VATs) and animate hundreds or thousands of instanced characters with zero per-frame CPU: one draw call per material, no `SkinnedMesh` per character. One baked VAT renders on both `WebGLRenderer` (GLSL) and `WebGPURenderer` (TSL). ESM only, `three >= 0.186` peer dependency, Node >= 20.

The whole integration is four calls: `bakeVAT` (from `three-vat`) once at load, `createVATMesh` (from `three-vat/webgl` or `three-vat/tsl`, and that import is the only line that differs between renderers), `setMatrixAt` for placement, and `time.value = clock.getElapsedTime()` once per frame. Changing what one instance plays later is one `setVATInstance(playback, index, instance)` write; there is no mixer, no `update(dt)`, and no per-frame loop over instances.

Rules an assistant writing code for this library most often gets wrong:

- Pass the subtree root (`gltf.scene`) to `bakeVAT`, never a `SkinnedMesh` found inside it.
- Render `vat.geometry` (what `createVATMesh` does). Never the source mesh's geometry: the textures are indexed by the baker's vertex order.
- Import `bakeVAT` from `three-vat`; import `createVATMesh` and `getMaxTextureSize` from `three-vat/webgl` or `three-vat/tsl`. The root entry point has no `createVATMesh`.
- `startTime` is an absolute time on the same clock you write into `time.value`. Desync a crowd with `startTime: -Math.random() * 2`, not with a time offset field (none exists since 2.0).
- Pass `maxTextureSize: getMaxTextureSize(renderer)` to `bakeVAT`. On WebGPU call it after `await renderer.init()`.
- Draw calls equal material count, not instance count. `mergeFlatMaterials: true` collapses colour-only materials into one.
- The default end mode is `EndMode.Clamp` (holds the last frame), unlike three's `clampWhenFinished = false`.
- It does not do LOD, IK, blend trees (more than two clips at once), or React/drei bindings.

A complete, self-contained reference with every export, signature and pitfall is [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/llms-full.txt). Read it before writing non-trivial code.

## Docs

- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/llms-full.txt): the full API reference and pitfalls in one file, written for LLMs
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/README.md): install and one crowd, start to finish
- [Usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/docs/usage.md): texture ceilings, encodings, draw calls, workers, the CLI and baked files, loop modes, crossfades, turns, BatchedMesh, spawning, custom GLSL
- [Glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/CONTEXT.md): the domain vocabulary (VAT, bake, clip, frame, slot, carrier, playback texture, crossfade, turn)
- [CHANGELOG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/CHANGELOG.md): breaking changes by version, including the 1.x to 2.0 playback contract

## Examples

- [Live demo gallery](https://mikefernandez-pro.github.io/three-vat/): every example page, one per renderer
- [Examples index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/main/docs/examples.md): what each page demonstrates
- [webgl_crowd.html](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/webgl_crowd.html) / [webgpu_crowd.html](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/webgpu_crowd.html): the basic crowd, `bakeVAT` then `createVATMesh`, in one self-contained file ([webgl_crowd.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_crowd.ts))
- [webgl_instanced.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_instanced.ts) / [webgpu_instanced.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_instanced.ts): your own InstancedMesh wired by hand, with the playback texture and `patchVATMaterial` or `vatNodes`, a switch per step
- [webgl_clips.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_clips.ts) / [webgpu_clips.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_clips.ts): one instance's clip switched with `setVATInstance`, one row of the playback texture written
- [webgl_policy.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_policy.ts) / [webgpu_policy.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_policy.ts): loop mode, repetitions, end mode and speed, negative speed playing the band backwards
- [webgl_turn.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_turn.ts) / [webgpu_turn.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_turn.ts): `turnVATInstance`, walkers retracing their stride from the pose they show
- [webgl_crossfade.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_crossfade.ts) / [webgpu_crossfade.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_crossfade.ts): a `fadeDuration` crossfade, the clip left behind still playing under the blend
- [webgl_events.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_events.ts) / [webgpu_events.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_events.ts): `endsAt` scheduling a CPU-side event when a finite play finishes, with `resolveVATFrame` asked what the shader shows
- [webgl_encodings.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_encodings.ts) / [webgpu_encodings.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_encodings.ts): the rig encoding against the vertex encoding on a skinned character, their textures side by side at one scale
- [webgl_normals.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_normals.ts) / [webgpu_normals.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_normals.ts): `bakeNormals: false` under an unlit and a flat-shaded material, beside a lit one, and the lit one without normals
- [webgl_merged.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_merged.ts) / [webgpu_merged.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_merged.ts): `mergeFlatMaterials: true`, three materials drawn as one, with a swatch diagram read off the bake
- [webgl_large.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_large.ts) / [webgpu_large.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_large.ts): a 16 340-vertex mesh past the texture ceiling, `vat.rowsPerFrame`, the frame's rows lit on the texture
- [webgl_morph.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_morph.ts) / [webgpu_morph.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_morph.ts): the vertex encoding: morph-target and node animation, and an `'auto'` fallback with its reason on `vat.fallback`
- [webgl_worker.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_worker.ts) / [webgpu_worker.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_worker.ts): baking in a Web Worker with `bakeVATInWorker`
- [webgl_file.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_file.ts) / [webgpu_file.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_file.ts): a `.vat.glb` from the bake command, loaded with `loadVAT`
- [webgl_batched.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_batched.ts) / [webgpu_batched.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_batched.ts): a `BatchedMesh` crowd from a fixed capacity, spawning into the rows dead instances freed, one draw on both renderers
- [webgl_deform.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_deform.ts) / [webgpu_deform.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_deform.ts): your own deformation after the decode, the post-decode hook on WebGL and a graph round `positionNode` on WebGPU
- [webgl_shadows.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_shadows.ts) / [webgpu_shadows.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_shadows.ts): two soldiers side by side, one shadow matching the pose and one in the rest pose, `createVATDepthMaterial` on WebGL and `positionNode` in the shadow pass on WebGPU
- [webgl_drop.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgl_drop.ts) / [webgpu_drop.ts](https://github.com/MikeFernandez-Pro/three-vat/blob/main/examples/src/webgpu_drop.ts): bake your own glTF or FBX in a worker, download it as a baked file, or copy the code
